messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: P1 - serving-runtime error spike. Metric: cudaIllegalMemoryAccess on gpunode-04,gpunode-05. 15-25 errors/min. Auto-created INC-2026-082. Pager: sophia (oncall). Link: https://infra/redwood/incidents/INC-2026-082

sophia (oncall): seeing 502s from model shards on 4/5 GPUs in the pool. rolling restarts auto-failing. customer errors up ~18%. WFM to take initial triage.

arjun (eng-runtime): grabbing logs now. kernel oops mentions "misaligned address" in pagewalk, plus uvm faulting. possible pagemap race during live migration.

arjun (eng-runtime): attaching a trimmed dmesg/backtrace snippet:
```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 43, PID=2345 Read Error: GPU reported a fault during a VA space operation.
[ 1234.567895] BUG: unable to handle kernel NULL pointer dereference at 0000000000000000
[ 1234.567900] CPU: 3 PID: 2345 Comm: worker-serve Not tainted 5.15.0-rt1
[ 1234.567905] Call Trace:
  ffffffff810d2e1b 
  ffffffffc02b1d2a 
  ffffffffc02b4c77
```

tracy (eng-sre): ok, immediate mitigation steps: cordon gpunode-04 and gpunode-05, drain with --ignore-daemonsets, failover traffic. if drain stalls, force delete pods and scale up healthy nodes.

mike (support): prepping customer comms. Affected customers: 7 tenants, highest impact on batch inference (throughput jobs). ETA for initial update: 10m.

arjun (eng-runtime): quick triage findings:
- repeated cudaIllegalMemoryAccess correlates with kernel pagewalks during high prefetch/prefill activity.
- kv-cache invalidation spikes when we hot-reload model shards, causing concurrent VA mappings.

arjun (eng-runtime): immediate runtime mitigations I suggest:
1) disable shard hot-reload on pool for next 30m: set RELOAD_ON_START=false on deploys.
2) reduce prefetch window (batcher config) to minimal to avoid overlapping VA ops.
3) route a portion of traffic to cpu-fallback pool (model-fallback-small) to reduce pressure.

tracy (eng-sre): executing cordon/drain now:
`kubectl cordon gpunode-04 && kubectl drain gpunode-04 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force`
tracy (eng-sre): drain progressing, some pods stuck Terminating due to long kernel hang; forcing eviction.

incident-bot: ACTION TAKEN: nodes cordoned: gpunode-04,gpunode-05. Failover routing enabled to region-us-east-2 backup pool.

sophia (oncall): arjun — can you push the config change to disable hot-reload? I can babysit routing/fallback.

arjun (eng-runtime): pushed: `env override RELOAD_ON_START=false` to staging and prod pool. Deployed config with canary 5%.

arjun (eng-runtime): also lowered batcher prefetch from 32 -> 8 in live config. Monitoring for errors to drop.

mike (support): customer update sent: "We're aware of an elevated error rate caused by GPU memory faults; mitigation in progress, routing to fallback pools, ETA next update 20 minutes."

tracy (eng-sre): kernel oops persists on one worker; collecting /proc/kcore and full dmesg for triage. tagging research for kernel race analysis.

arjun (eng-runtime): temporary kernel workaround: disable device page-walk prefetch for our nv driver path (echo 0 > /sys/module/nvidia/parameters/prefetch_enabled) on affected nodes — doing this on gpunode-04 before we reboot.

sophia (oncall): copy that. Reboots planned after cordon/drain complete. Rolling reboots scheduled in 10m windows.

ops-bot: NOTE: scheduled restart of worker pool 'serve-west-gpu' at 03:08 UTC for gpunode-04.

arjun (eng-runtime): after config and prefetch change, error rate dropped from 22/min -> 3/min on healthy nodes. Still seeing 1-2 residual faults on a quarantined node.

mike (support): updated customers with degraded throughput but most requests now succeed via CPU fallback. No data loss reported.

sophia (oncall): handing off to arjun for longer-term (kernel/driver) investigation. I'm moving to secondary follow-up channel. I'll monitor customer comms for 2 hours.

arjun (eng-runtime): taking over. Next steps for triage:
- collect full kernel trace and perf record of pagewalks.
- reproduce with reduced batcher in staging and iterate on nv driver parameters.
- prepare a canary kernel patch/driver config to test on isolated node.

tracy (eng-sre): filing post-incident ticket: INC-2026-082-POST with root-cause hypothesis: concurrent VA remap + prefetch race causing misaligned pagewalk leading to CUDA illegal memory access. Attach logs and timestamps.

mike (support): final customer note queued for 1h: summary + mitigation + ETA on RCA.

arjun (eng-runtime): assigning: @tracy collect kernel traces; @li (research) to attempt reproducer with stressbench; @mike finalize customer comms; I'll own driver param testing.

sophia (oncall): thanks all. If anything changes please ping @here and escalate to SRE lead.

incident-bot: STATUS UPDATE: mitigated -> partial. Error rate reduced to baseline after routing + config changes. Incident remains open for RCA.

arjun (eng-runtime): leaving logs here for handoff to next oncall: s3://redwood-logs/INC-2026-082/ (full dmesg, kube events, pod logs). Handoff ETA: 03:30 UTC.

sophia (oncall): acknowledged handoff. Closing active page for my shift; follow-up owners assigned in ticket.

mike (support): marking customers notified. Will post the customer-facing timeline in the ticket when RCA draft is ready. :thumbsup:
